questions.stem: In any emergency your first priority is:
options: Saving the boat
Finding the cause
Protecting life
Saving cargo

questions.stem: After a grounding on a falling tide you should:
options: Go full astern before the water drops
You may be stuck until the tide rises again
Open the sea valves to lighten her
Shift everyone forward to lift the stern off the bottom

questions.stem: After a grounding, before trying to refloat you should:
options: Switch off the radio
Check for damage and flooding
Immediately go full astern
Fill the tanks with water
questions.explanation: Power can pull out a plug.

questions.stem: If the other vessel's bow is plugging a hole in your hull after a collision, you should:
options: Open the throttle to push in harder
Back away at once so you can see the damage
Keep it there until you can assess the damage
Abandon ship straight away
questions.explanation: It may be keeping you afloat.

questions.stem: In a boat fire you should if possible:
options: Keep going at speed so the wind blows the fire out
Put the fire downwind and shut off fuel
Turn so the fire is upwind of you
Open the windows to let smoke out
questions.explanation: Smoke and flames then blow away from you.

options: The top of the flames
The thickest smoke
The cabin ceiling
The base of the flames
questions.explanation: PASS: pull, aim at base, squeeze, sweep.

options: You want a tow in good weather
There is grave and imminent danger
You are running late for a booking
You are unsure of your position
questions.explanation: Use Pan-Pan for urgent but not life-threatening.

questions.stem: To control flooding you should first:
options: Find and stop the source and start pumps
Open more valves to let it drain
Keep going at full speed to lift the bow
Call ashore and wait for advice

questions.stem: Which should be done early in an emergency?
options: Remove lifejackets
Put lifejackets on everyone
Hide the flares
Wait for the situation to worsen
questions.explanation: Do it before you need it.
